92:             "Reference velocities must have the same length as "
93:             "pitches and intervals."
94:         )
95:     if not est_velocities.shape[0] == est_pitches.shape[0]:
96:         raise ValueError(
97:             "Estimated velocities must have the same length as "
98:             "pitches and intervals."
99:         )
100:     # Check that the velocities are positive
101:     if ref_velocities.size > 0 and np.min(ref_velocities) < 0:
102:         raise ValueError("Reference velocities must be positive.")
103:     if est_velocities.size > 0 and np.min(est_velocities) < 0:
104:         raise ValueError("Estimated velocities must be positive.")
105: 
106: 
107: def match_notes(
108:     ref_intervals,
109:     ref_pitches,
110:     ref_velocities,
111:     est_intervals,
112:     est_pitches,
113:     est_velocities,
114:     onset_tolerance=0.05,
115:     pitch_tolerance=50.0,
116:     offset_ratio=0.2,
117:     offset_min_tolerance=0.05,
118:     strict=False,
119:     velocity_tolerance=0.1,
120: ):
121:     """Match notes, taking note velocity into consideration.
122: 
123:     This function first calls :func:`mir_eval.transcription.match_notes` to
124:     match notes according to the supplied intervals, pitches, onset, offset,
125:     and pitch tolerances. The velocities of the matched notes are then used to
126:     estimate a slope and intercept which can rescale the estimated velocities
127:     so that they are as close as possible (in L2 sense) to their matched
128:     reference velocities. Velocities are then normalized to the range [0, 1]. A
129:     estimated note is then further only considered correct if its velocity is
130:     within ``velocity_tolerance`` of its matched (according to pitch and
131:     timing) reference note.
132: 
133:     Parameters
134:     ----------
135:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n,2)
136:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
137:     ref_pitches : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
138:         Array of reference pitch values in Hertz
139:     ref_velocities : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
140:         Array of MIDI velocities (i.e. between 0 and 127) of reference notes
141:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
142:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
143:     est_pitches : np.ndarray, shape=(m,)
144:         Array of estimated pitch values in Hertz
145:     est_velocities : np.ndarray, shape=(m,)
146:         Array of MIDI velocities (i.e. between 0 and 127) of estimated notes
147:     onset_tolerance : float > 0
148:         The tolerance for an estimated note's onset deviating from the
149:         reference note's onset, in seconds. Default is 0.05 (50 ms).
150:     pitch_tolerance : float > 0
151:         The tolerance for an estimated note's pitch deviating from the
152:         reference note's pitch, in cents. Default is 50.0 (50 cents).
153:     offset_ratio : float > 0 or None
154:         The ratio of the reference note's duration used to define the
155:         offset_tolerance. Default is 0.2 (20%), meaning the
156:         ``offset_tolerance`` will equal the ``ref_duration * 0.2``, or 0.05 (50
157:         ms), whichever is greater. If ``offset_ratio`` is set to ``None``,
158:         offsets are ignored in the matching.
159:     offset_min_tolerance : float > 0
160:         The minimum tolerance for offset matching. See offset_ratio description
161:         for an explanation of how the offset tolerance is determined. Note:
162:         this parameter only influences the results if ``offset_ratio`` is not
163:         ``None``.
164:     strict : bool
165:         If ``strict=False`` (the default), threshold checks for onset, offset,
166:         and pitch matching are performed using ``<=`` (less than or equal). If
167:         ``strict=True``, the threshold checks are performed using ``<`` (less
168:         than).
169:     velocity_tolerance : float > 0
170:         Estimated notes are considered correct if, after rescaling and
171:         normalization to [0, 1], they are within ``velocity_tolerance`` of a
172:         matched reference note.
173: 
174:     Returns
175:     -------
176:     matching : list of tuples
177:         A list of matched reference and estimated notes.
178:         ``matching[i] == (i, j)`` where reference note ``i`` matches estimated
179:         note ``j``.
180:     """
181:     # Compute note matching as usual using standard transcription function
182:     matching = transcription.match_notes(
183:         ref_intervals,
184:         ref_pitches,
185:         est_intervals,
186:         est_pitches,
187:         onset_tolerance,
188:         pitch_tolerance,
189:         offset_ratio,
190:         offset_min_tolerance,
191:         strict,
192:     )
193: 
194:     # Rescale reference velocities to the range [0, 1]
195:     min_velocity, max_velocity = np.min(ref_velocities), np.max(ref_velocities)
196:     # Make the smallest possible range 1 to avoid divide by zero
197:     velocity_range = max(1, max_velocity - min_velocity)
198:     ref_velocities = (ref_velocities - min_velocity) / float(velocity_range)
199: 
200:     # Convert matching list-of-tuples to array for fancy indexing
201:     matching = np.array(matching)
202:     # When there is no matching, return an empty list
203:     if matching.size == 0:
204:         return []
205:     # Grab velocities for matched notes
206:     ref_matched_velocities = ref_velocities[matching[:, 0]]
207:     est_matched_velocities = est_velocities[matching[:, 1]]
208:     # Find slope and intercept of line which produces best least-squares fit
209:     # between matched est and ref velocities
210:     slope, intercept = np.linalg.lstsq(
211:         np.vstack([est_matched_velocities, np.ones(len(est_matched_velocities))]).T,
212:         ref_matched_velocities,
213:         rcond=None,
214:     )[0]
215:     # Re-scale est velocities to match ref
216:     est_matched_velocities = slope * est_matched_velocities + intercept
217:     # Compute the absolute error of (rescaled) estimated velocities vs.
218:     # normalized reference velocities. Error will be in [0, 1]
219:     velocity_diff = np.abs(est_matched_velocities - ref_matched_velocities)
220:     # Check whether each error is within the provided tolerance
221:     velocity_within_tolerance = velocity_diff < velocity_tolerance
222:     # Only keep matches whose velocity was within the provided tolerance
223:     matching = matching[velocity_within_tolerance]
224:     # Convert back to list-of-tuple format
225:     matching = [tuple(_) for _ in matching]
226: 
227:     return matching
228: 
229: 
230: def precision_recall_f1_overlap(
231:     ref_intervals,
232:     ref_pitches,
233:     ref_velocities,
234:     est_intervals,
235:     est_pitches,
236:     est_velocities,
237:     onset_tolerance=0.05,
238:     pitch_tolerance=50.0,
239:     offset_ratio=0.2,
240:     offset_min_tolerance=0.05,
241:     strict=False,
242:     velocity_tolerance=0.1,
243:     beta=1.0,
244: ):
245:     """Compute the Precision, Recall and F-measure of correct vs incorrectly
246:     transcribed notes, and the Average Overlap Ratio for correctly transcribed
247:     notes (see :func:`mir_eval.transcription.average_overlap_ratio`).
